name: cavemio-changelog-scrubber
title: Changelog scrubber
description: Your release history on a ruler you scrub: drag the playhead, or press play and watch the product ship.

cavemio.accessibility:
- The ruler is a slider: arrow keys step between releases, Home and End jump to the first and the latest, and its value reads as the version, title and date.
- Play is a real button whose label changes between "Play the releases" and "Pause"; dragging, swiping, the arrows or a key pause it.
- On touch the ruler takes the whole gesture, like any slider. The card takes only sideways swipes; vertical ones still scroll the page.
- The arrows are buttons labelled "Older release" and "Newer release"; at either end they are aria-disabled rather than disabled, so focus stays on them.
- The lens is CSS: each tick reads the playhead’s position from one custom property and works out its own height, so a frame of scrubbing is one style write and no layout. Frames run only while the playhead moves.
- Installs Number roll and Text morph. Uses container query units (cqw), in every current browser. With reduced motion the playhead jumps instead of gliding and play steps from release to release.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: entries
props.description: – · Newest first: id, date, title, and any of version, tags, body, media. The ruler spaces them by date.

props.name: value
props.description: – · The release on show, by id (controlled).

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: the newest · Where it opens when uncontrolled. A link to #<id> opens on that release.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: – · Called as the release changes, including while scrubbing and playing.

props.name: playDuration
props.description: 1200 × releases · How long play takes from the first release to the latest, in ms.

props.name: locales
props.description: "en-GB" · How dates and month names read.

features.title: A ruler spaced by date
features.description: Releases sit on a thin line ruler of days, so a quick month and a quiet one look different.

features.title: Scrub, click or step
features.description: Drag the playhead, click the ruler or press an arrow key. The version, date and tag morph and the release slides in.

features.title: Play the history
features.description: Press play and the releases run at the pace they shipped, from where you are to the latest.

features.title: Smooth on a phone
features.description: Swipe the card to step through, and a frame of scrubbing costs one style write.

features.title: Linkable releases
features.description: A link to #release-id opens the scrubber on that release.

features.title: A real slider
features.description: Arrow keys, Home and End work, and the value reads as the version, title and date.

states.title: scrub
states.description: The playhead follows the pointer exactly. Ticks within 7% of the ruler either side swell up to 2.6× (release marks 1.45×) on a smooth falloff, and the card switches to the nearest release as you cross the midpoint between two.

states.title: settle
states.description: On release, a click or an arrow key, the playhead is thrown onto the release (520ms, slight overshoot) and its mark darkens.

states.title: change
states.description: The version on the playhead, the date and the tag morph letter by letter, "3 of 7" rolls, and the release slides 24px in from the side the playhead moved toward through a 6px blur (460ms) while the old one leaves the other way. The card’s height eases to the new release (460ms).

states.title: play
states.description: The playhead runs from where it is to the latest release at one speed (1.2s a release on average), so a busy week flicks past and a quiet month takes its time. Play from the end starts again at the first release. The icon blurs between play and pause.

states.title: swipe
states.description: On touch, the release follows your finger (0.8×, or 0.3× past the first or last). A swipe past 56px or a quick flick moves one release and the old one carries on from where you let go; anything less springs back (420ms, slight overshoot).

states.title: step
states.description: The arrows beside the count step one release. At the first or last, that arrow fades to 30% and does nothing.

states.title: hover
states.description: With a mouse, a faint line shows where a click would land.
